It's more of a metaphor. He's not saying "If any dog doesn't want to come near you, you must evaluate yourself." He's using a dog as a metaphor for something usually considered (even more so back then than now) dirty, lesser and morally ambiguous. The idea is that, if something like that won't even come near you (something dirty, morally corrupt, wrong) then you may have a problem. He's not literally referring to if an actual dog won't come up to you then you're a bad person.

It's like when people say, "the devil wouldn't even hang out with that person." They aren't saying that the devil doesn't find that person to be fun or cool, it's a statement on the persons character. The idea that said person is so evil/mean/bad/corrupt, that even something as evil as the devil wouldn't want to go near them.
In that light, it makes more sense... I still can't say I wholly agree with it, but I'm not one to nitpick sayings. I'll accept it as is. Thanks for defining it better.
